finding.claim: Stored user-supplied callbackUrl is fetched server-side by a scheduled job with no host or address validation, enabling blind SSRF to internal or metadata endpoints via POST.
finding.source: callbackUrl argument of Jobs.subscribe (Jobs.java:13), stored unvalidated at Jobs.java:14; reached via POST /subscribe (route not in repo, auth UNCERTAIN)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) in Jobs.notifyAll (Jobs.java:24), with URI.create(cb) at Jobs.java:21

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) accepts raw URL from the request body
subscriptions.put stores the URL with no validation
notifyAll(payload) invoked on a per-minute schedule (comment at line 17)
iterates over all stored callback URLs
POST with payload body to the attacker-chosen URL
client.send issues the request; response body read and discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No host, IP, or private-range filter. Scheme is limited to http/https by HttpRequest.Builder.uri. Redirects are not followed (HttpClient.newHttpClient defaults to Redirect.NEVER). URI.create only rejects malformed syntax. Route auth for /subscribe is not visible in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. No host, IP, or scheme validation exists on the path in src/Jobs.java (subscribe at :13-15, notifyAll at :18-25, URI.create at :21). The only validation in the file is in thumb() at :30, which is not on this path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out: subscribe stores the raw callbackUrl at Jobs.java:14, notifyAll POSTs to each stored URL at :21-24, and the scheduling comment is at :17. The sink is not closed by any guard. Attacker control is unverified, though: the only evidence that callbackUrl comes from a remote POST /subscribe body is the comment at Jobs.java:12, and the route handler and its auth are not in the repo, so I cannot tell whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege user can reach this value. If the route is exposed to any non-admin user, this becomes CONFIRMED.
